referents.why: 'his heart' (third masculine singular possessive) is Pharaoh's: the hardening is his.
masculine plural object 'them' of 'would not listen to': Moses and Aaron, the composite of the two named in this verse.
third masculine singular 'he would not listen': the subject of the hardening and refusal is Pharaoh.

links.why: 'he saw that there was relief': that after a verb of seeing introduces what is seen.
cl1 is the object of cl0's seeing, not an event that follows it; the narrative line runs from cl0 to cl2.
a separate-word waw joins two acts of Pharaoh. The text does not say the hardening results from seeing the relief.
R4 gives this pair as a will hardened, then the refusal that follows, which is result rather than and.
'he hardened his heart' and then 'would not listen to them': the refusal is what the hardening brings about (R4).
'just as the LORD had said': a comparison to a saying, which declares the refusal the fulfilment of an earlier word.
